formation.explanation: RawNode.Propose or serialized Node loop enters the role-specific state machine. A leader admits entries, assigns term/index and appends locally; a follower forwards only with leader knowledge and enabled forwarding, while a candidate drops. Leader self support is queued, and follower MsgApp validates previous term and reconciles only an uncommitted suffix before queueing its response. send places append/vote responses behind persistence. Async MsgStorageAppend carries responses requiring ordered durable writes; synchronous Ready.Messages and Advance carry corresponding duties. Positive responses increase per-peer Match; configured majority order statistics (minimum of both groups for joint configuration) supply an index, and maybeCommit additionally matches the current term. Commit propagates through append and heartbeat; heartbeat commit is capped by recipient Match. Followers commit matching received prefixes and do not overwrite committed entries. Ready exposes committed entries, with async mode limited to stable local history and all modes pausing entries behind snapshots. The embedding state machine applies them in order, activates config entries, and correlates its own client completion. A successful proposal call has no commitment guarantee.

context.explanation: An election timeout or Campaign starts only for a locally eligible nonlearner without pending snapshot or unapplied committed configuration. Pre-vote leaves term/vote unchanged; real campaign increments term and queues its self vote until persistence. Voters check vote eligibility and last-log ordering; phase-specific replies are tallied once per sender over active voter sets. A won result establishes local leadership, resets replication tracking and appends an empty current-term entry. Higher-term traffic generally steps the node down, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions; lower-term traffic is rejected before normal role consumers. CheckQuorum can remove leadership after insufficient recent voter activity. Transfer pauses proposals, catches up an eligible transferee, sends TimeoutNow, and aborts after an election timeout. Membership activation changes voter sets and local promotability; removal stepdown is configurable. Restart rebuilds from storage HardState and ConfState as follower. Snapshot restore accepts a newer committed prefix with recipient membership, either fast-forwarding a matching log or installing snapshot and reconstructed configuration.

connection.explanation: Authority reset clears tally, peer Match, and heartbeat read acknowledgments but preserves log and committed/application positions; old uncommitted entries can be replaced only above committed. Current-term entry commitment requalifies retained earlier log history. Configuration application changes eligibility of retained Progress, while new members start Match zero and joint votes/commits require both majorities. Queued persistence responses retain original RPC context: stale network replies cannot enter normal consumers, and stale append-thread entry acknowledgments cannot release unstable entries even if entry identities recur. A new-term HardState-only append can reconfirm in-progress history; snapshot and application completions remain term-independent because they concern committed state. Pending reads waiting for the first current-term commit survive reset, then receive a new commit index and new heartbeat acknowledgments in safe mode; already collected readOnly acknowledgments do not survive. ReadState is only a request-specific application-read prerequisite. Committed configuration application also governs campaign eligibility, and automatic joint exit follows applied progress.

feedback.answered: README repeats same-batch concurrent send wording, but independently requires Entries before changed HardState. Ready.Messages remains stricter and raft.send explicitly describes append acknowledgments as persistence-dependent. Therefore a generic immediate-send scenario with a HardState update would not isolate the ambiguity. The selected experiment instead requires an unchanged follower HardState and produces every network response through the implementation.
